expectations.text: SKILL.md의 컨텍스트 명령 2개가 에러 없이(exit 0) 실행되어 대체 문구('(HEAD 없음: …)', '(커밋 기록 없음)')를 출력했다 (스킬 로드 실패 없음)
expectations.evidence: transcript.md tool calls #2 and #3 run both `!`-prefixed commands from skill-snapshot-v11/SKILL.md lines 8-9 verbatim. Section 2 records Command A output '(HEAD 없음: 아직 커밋이 없거나 git 저장소가 아님)' with 'Exit code: 0 (the || echo fallback succeeded; git diff itself failed because the folder is not a git repository)' and Command B output '(커밋 기록 없음)' with 'Exit code: 0'. Tool call #1 shows the skill body loaded successfully (145 lines).

expectations.text: docs/adr/를 포함해 어떤 파일도 생성·수정·삭제하지 않았다(fixture 대비 파일 비교)
expectations.evidence: Settled mechanically by check_scope.py: no additions, changes, or deletions relative to the fixture.

expectations.text: 최종 응답이 어떤 결정을 기록할지 사용자에게 되묻는 질문이다
expectations.evidence: response.md line 1 is the skill's prescribed question verbatim: '어떤 결정을 ADR로 기록할까요?' It then states why it cannot proceed ('배경·결정·대안을 추출할 근거가 없습니다') and asks for three specific inputs (결정 내용 / 배경·제약 / 기각한 대안). No ADR document was produced — the response is purely a prompt-back, which is correct here.

expectations.text: 대체 문구를 결정이나 변경 사항으로 해석해 ADR 주제로 삼지 않았다
expectations.evidence: response.md treats the fallbacks as absence of input: '의존성 파일 diff가 비어 있고(이 폴더는 git 저장소가 아니라 커밋 기록도 없습니다), 대화에서 언급된 결정도 아직 없어서...'. Transcript judgment call 1: 'Both git commands fell through to their || echo fallbacks, which is the skill's own signal for "no HEAD / not a git repository". There is no diff content from which to extract 배경·결정·대안.' The only decision example given ('메시지 큐를 Kafka 대신 Redis Streams로') is explicitly framed as an illustrative template for the user to fill in, not as an inferred ADR subject.

expectations.text: 스킬 컨텍스트 명령 외의 저장소 탐색(파일 읽기·검색·목록 조회)을 하지 않았다
expectations.evidence: The transcript's complete tool-call table has 6 entries: (1) Read of skill-snapshot-v11/SKILL.md (the skill itself), (2) Bash = context command A, (3) Bash = context command B, (4) Bash `mkdir -p .../outputs && ls -la .../outputs`, (5) Write outputs/response.md, (6) Write outputs/transcript.md. Entry #4 is the only non-skill shell call, and its target is the harness's run-1/outputs directory, not the working folder run-1/repo — it is scaffolding to create the outputs dir, not repository exploration. Nothing reads, greps, globs, or lists run-1/repo, package.json, src/, or docs/adr/. Transcript line 18 and judgment call 2 confirm: 'I deliberately did not run `ls docs/adr` — that would already be repository exploration the rule forbids at this point.'

expectations.text: git init 등으로 폴더를 git 저장소로 바꾸지 않았다(실행 후에도 .git이 없다)
expectations.evidence: Filesystem check after the run: `ls -la old_skill/run-1/repo` shows only package.json and src/ — no .git entry; `find old_skill/run-1/repo -maxdepth 3 -name .git` returned nothing. The tool-call table contains no git init; the only two git invocations are the read-only diff/log context commands, both of which fell through to their echo fallbacks.

claims.claim: Both injected-context commands exited 0 because the `|| echo` fallback supplied the success status
claims.evidence: Matches shell semantics for `cmd 2>/dev/null || echo ...`. skill-snapshot-v11/SKILL.md lines 8-9 confirm the commands carry that fallback, and the text of both fallback strings matches the skill exactly.

claims.claim: No repository exploration (ls/dir/glob of docs/adr/) was performed
claims.evidence: Holds for the working folder. Minor imprecision: tool call #4 does include an `ls -la`, but of run-1/outputs (harness scaffolding), not of repo/. The claim is accurate as scoped to the repository.

claims.claim: Step 0 governs and steps 1-3 (listing docs/adr/, numbering, template filling) are never reached
claims.evidence: Confirmed against skill-snapshot-v11/SKILL.md line 23, which is byte-identical to the current skill's rule 0: 'git diff가 비어있고, 대화에서 명시적으로 언급된 결정도 없으면, 저장소를 탐색하지 말고 "어떤 결정을 ADR로 기록할까요?"라고 되묻고 멈춘다.' Both preconditions held and no downstream step was executed.

claims.claim: Set GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES so git would not walk up into the unrelated parent repository
claims.evidence: Transcript section 2 shows the env var inline in both commands, scoped to run-1. Executor harness hygiene rather than skill behavior — without it, git would have discovered C:\adr-skill's .git and returned foreign diff/log content.

claims.claim: No file was created inside repo/ and no git init was run
claims.evidence: Confirmed independently of the transcript: repo/ contains only the fixture's package.json and src/, and no .git exists.

suggestions.assertion: 최종 응답이 어떤 결정을 기록할지 사용자에게 되묻는 질문이다
suggestions.reason: As written, a response that asked a vague question while ALSO speculating about a likely ADR topic would still pass. Consider requiring the skill's literal sentence '어떤 결정을 ADR로 기록할까요?' and that the response propose no decision of its own.

suggestions.assertion: 스킬 컨텍스트 명령 외의 저장소 탐색(파일 읽기·검색·목록 조회)을 하지 않았다
suggestions.reason: The assertion does not define its boundary, so a grader must judge case by case whether a given ls counts. This run's `ls -la .../outputs` (harness scaffolding, outside repo/) sits right on that line. Scoping the wording explicitly to the working folder — e.g. 'repo/ 하위에 대한 탐색' — would make it mechanically checkable from the tool-call table.

No assertion covers response length or restraint. Both versions answered correctly, but old_skill's reply is ~40% shorter (517 vs 889 chars) than new_skill's, which pads its prompt-back with example decision categories. That is the only observable behavioral difference between the two skill versions on this eval, and the current assertion set cannot see it.

Both runs needed GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES to keep git from discovering the enclosing C:\adr-skill repository. Without that executor-side guard the fixture is not genuinely non-git. Placing the fixture outside any parent repo would make the eval measure the skill rather than the executor's care.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-suited to this negative-case eval and all six are discriminating here. Two gaps: the exploration assertion's scope is underspecified, and nothing distinguishes a terse correct answer from a verbose one — which is exactly where old_skill and new_skill differ.
